interest: For historians of interwar international relations and military buildup, this file offers valuable insight into the commercial and diplomatic dimensions of Japanese rearmament prior to the Pacific War. It illustrates how Japan actively sought advanced Western aeronautical and navigation technology—from high-power British Rolls-Royce Buzzard engines to American radio beacon transmitters—while Western governments maintained permissive export policies in the absence of explicit statutory embargoes or military secret classifications. Additionally, the military intelligence report on base development in the Kurile Islands illuminates early strategic rivalry and base competition between Japan and the United States across the North Pacific-Aleutian axis in the early 1930s.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.348, covering November 1931 to September 1934) documents Japanese efforts to procure foreign aviation technology and equipment, as well as intelligence on Japanese naval aviation expansion in the North Pacific. The file contains records concerning Japan's purchase of ten Rolls-Royce Buzzard aircraft engines from Great Britain despite inquiries in the House of Commons regarding an international arms embargo; an inquiry by the Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company regarding the potential sale of commercial radio beacon transmitters to a Japanese Naval Mission following an inspection in Elizabeth, New Jersey; and a C-2 military intelligence report detailing Admiral Kōichi Shiozawa's inspection of the Kurile Islands to establish naval air bases to counter American base development in the Aleutian Islands of Alaska.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting London Embassy Despatch No. 1951 concerning Japanese orders for aeroplane engines and naval aircraft in Great Britain.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State Document File Note (cross-reference sheet) referencing Despatch No. 1951, dated November 30, 1931, sent by Ray Atherton from Great Britain and filed under 841.00 P.R./208. It records a statement made by the British Prime Minister in the House of Commons on November 24th regarding orders for aeroplane engines and naval aircraft placed in Great Britain by Japan. The sheet indexes the transaction under State Department decimal file 894.348/11.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 1951 Regarding Aeroplane Engines for Japan

subfiles.about: Extract from a London Embassy despatch reporting on British policy regarding aircraft engine exports to Japan and the purchase of Rolls-Royce engines.
subfiles.summary: An extract (page 15) from London Embassy Despatch No. 1951 reporting on a parliamentary exchange in the House of Commons on November 24, 1931. When asked whether he would consider placing an international embargo on orders for aeroplane engines and naval aircraft placed by Japan, the Prime Minister refused to adopt the proposal. The extract also notes reliable intelligence that Japan had ordered ten 825-horsepower Buzzard engines from the Rolls-Royce Company.
subfiles.title: Extract from Despatch No. 1951 on British Aeroplane Engines for Japan

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation between Joseph C. Green and Westinghouse representative Mr. Yanka regarding the possible purchase of radio beacon transmitters by Japan.
subfiles.summary: Joseph C. Green of the Division of Western European Affairs records a discussion with Mr. Yanka of the Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company regarding Japanese interest in radio beacon transmitters. Yanka inquired whether the Department of State had any objection to a Japanese Naval Mission inspecting and potentially purchasing beacon transmitters similar to the installation in Elizabeth, New Jersey. Green advised that no treaties or statutes prohibited such sales to Japan, provided no War or Navy Department military secrets were involved, which Yanka confirmed was not the case due to prior public and Bureau of Standards releases.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Proposed Japanese Purchase of Beacon Transmitters

subfiles.about: Military intelligence report quoting a British press report on Admiral Shiozawa inspecting the Kurile Islands for potential naval air base sites.
subfiles.summary: A C-2 military intelligence report (No. 36306) forwarded by the U.S. Military Attaché in London transmitting an excerpt from the Daily Herald of September 5, 1933. It reports that Admiral Kōichi Shiozawa, head of the Japanese naval air arm, was inspecting the Kurile Islands in the North Pacific to evaluate sites for naval air bases to counteract American base projects in the Aleutian Islands of Alaska. The report adds that Japan had allocated $2,000,000 for a purported fishing base equipped with a radio station and hospital suitable for wartime use.
subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Report on Japanese Naval Air Base Inspection in the Kurile Islands
